assumptions: Assay capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation are available and sensitive enough for fraction-level measurements.
A suitable exogenous intact-EV spike-in is available (distinct tracer to avoid overlap with endogenous markers) and behaves similarly to endogenous EVs in capture/protection assays.
This proposal does not assert efficacy or validated mechanism; it concerns product identity only.
biological_rationale: MISEV2023 underscores the need for orthogonal intact-EV analytics and controls to distinguish vesicular from non-vesicular signals. Existing program experiments propose capture+particle+detergent/protease workflows but lack an internal intact-EV recovery control that rules out assay or labeling loss as a competing explanation for negative capture co-localization. Introducing an exogenous, traceable intact-EV spike-in (isotope- or non-overlapping species marker) permits separating true absence of membrane-protected EV signal from assay recovery failure and provides an immediate, within-sample benchmark for intact-EV-associated identity assessment. This strengthens inference about whether a preparation is EV-enriched versus primarily secretome while remaining agnostic about potency.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Presence/absence qualitative gate: endogenous capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity in bounded fraction with concurrent preserved spike-in membrane-protected recovery in same fraction; not numeric release.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: EV identity and purity
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: An orthogonal identity gate that includes exogenous intact-EV spike-in recovery controls reduces ambiguity from assay loss and labeling artifacts when deciding whether the preparation is EV-enriched versus secretome.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: Moderate: spike-in control strengthens assay interpretation but does not by itself prove in vivo delivery or potency.

edges.competing_explanation: Spike-in recovery could be preserved while endogenous EVs are lost during processing; preserved spike-in recovery does not strictly prove endogenous particle integrity but does validate assay performance.
edges.missing_experiment: A paired spike-in recovery + endogenous capture co-localization experiment across bounded fraction and secretome controls.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends orthogonal controls; program rodent data indicate activity but do not link to spike-in-controlled intact-EV identity.

edges.competing_explanation: Endogenous capture-negative outcome in bounded fraction could reflect species- or route-specific loss rather than fractionation failure.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo bridging with spike-in controlled identity verification in lavage/CSF/tissue.
edges.model_or_species: non-human primate (contextual relevance for delivery uncertainty)
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: large-animal negative biodistribution motivates rigorous identity gating before bridging studies; species differences remain a competing explanation.

nodes.statement: If an exogenous, characterized intact-EV spike-in is recovered in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions and shows membrane-protection (loss after detergent/protease), then the orthogonal assay functions and negative endogenous capture co-localization reflects absence of intact EV enrichment rather than assay failure.

If the bounded small-EV fraction shows both (A) robust spike-in intact-EV recovery in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions and (B) endogenous capture-positive, detergent/protease-sensitive co-localizing signal, then the preparation can be classified as EV-enriched for drug-substance definition.

If concentrated conditioned medium lacks endogenous capture-positive, particle-peak co-localization despite preserved spike-in recovery, then the preparation is indistinguishable from secretome with non-vesicular co-isolates and should not be treated as an EV-enriched drug-substance.

competing_explanations: A preserved spike-in recovery could mask selective loss of a subpopulation of endogenous EVs that are the true active species.
Negative endogenous capture co-localization could result from donor/source-cell variability or downstream process damage that differentially affects endogenous versus spike-in particles.
dependencies: Define and source a characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in (distinct tracer) and its QC envelope
Ensure capture reagents with non-interfering buffer compatibility panels are available
Generate >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots from the same source-cell bank/passage to test reproducibility
design_question: Daily question: Can adding an exogenous, isotope-labeled intact-EV recovery control to conditioned-medium-derived preparations, then measuring its membrane-protected recovery (immuno-capture co-localized with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) at the fraction level, discriminate a bounded EV-enriched drug-substance from an unpurified secretome while controlling for assay recovery and labeling artifacts?
expected_measurable_effect: Qualitative assay pass: (1) spike-in intact-EV is recovered in capture-positive particle-peak fractions and shows loss after detergent+protease (demonstrating assay function), and (2) endogenous capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity is observed in bounded small-EV fraction but not in secretome-retaining concentrate from the same conditioned-medium lot.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal workflow combining: (1) add exogenous intact-EV spike-in to each sample prior to fractionation; (2) fractionate (iodixanol or SEC) and measure particle counts per fraction; (3) perform immuno-capture on intact fractions and quantify endogenous marker signal and spike-in tracer signal separately (distinct tracer readout); (4) perform protease/RNase protection with and without detergent on captured material for both spike-in tracer and endogenous signal; (5) measure total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction.
experiment.comparator: Matched pair from the same conditioned-medium lot: (A) bounded EV-enriched fraction spiked with exogenous intact-EV control versus (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) spiked identically. Include detergent+protease-treated aliquots and buffer-only negative controls. Spike-in enables within-sample recovery control.
experiment.control: Negative controls: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted samples. Positive control: characterized small EV preparation (commercial or lab-validated) spiked into buffer processed in parallel to verify capture and protection assay performance.
dependencies: Availability of consistent source-cell conditioned-medium lots (same passage/bank) for >=3 replicates
Access to a characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in with orthogonal tracer readout
Validated capture reagents and particle counting instrumentation
Laboratory capability for density-fractionation or SEC and protection assays
experiment.failure_criterion: Either (A) preserved spike-in recovery but no reproducible endogenous capture-positive co-localization in bounded fractions across replicates (endogenous signal absent despite validated assay), falsifying the hypothesis that the preparation is EV-enriched, or (B) inconsistent or absent spike-in membrane-protected recovery across replicates, preventing assay-controlled discrimination (methodology failure).
experiment.falsification_outcome: If spike-in recovery is confirmed but endogenous capture-positive co-localization is not observed reproducibly in bounded fractions across independent lots, treat the material as indistinguishable from secretome for identity and proceed to secretome-centric CMC strategy or alternative fractionation. If spike-in control fails, revise the control design or assay before relying on orthogonal identity gating.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: An orthogonal intact-EV identity gate consisting of (1) exogenous intact-EV spike-in membrane-protected recovery co-localized with particle peaks and capture-positive fractions, and (2) endogenous capture-positive, detergent/protease-sensitive co-localization with particle peaks in the bounded small-EV fraction but not in concentrated secretome, will discriminate an EV-enriched drug-substance candidate from secretome-retaining material.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative co-localization: particle-count peak fractions that are capture-positive and show (A) preserved spike-in tracer signal that is lost after detergent+protease (validating assay recovery and membrane protection) and (B) endogenous capture-positive signal that co-localizes with particle peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive in bounded fraction but not in secretome control.
experiment.question: Does adding a characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in before fractionation enable discrimination between a bounded EV-enriched fraction and a secretome-retaining conditioned-medium concentrate by demonstrating (A) spike-in membrane-protected recovery in capture-positive particle-peak fractions and (B) endogenous capture-positive, detergent/protease-sensitive co-localization in the bounded fraction but not in secretome control?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed as: (A) bounded small-EV enrichment (e.g., TFF->SEC->single-step iodixanol cushion) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium without enrichment (secretome-retaining)
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in (non-overlapping species or isotope-labeled tracer, QC-characterized for particle counts and marker display)
Immuno-capture reagents for canonical EV markers (anti-CD63, anti-CD9, anti-CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5)
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent) for membrane disruption
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
Buffers and blocking reagents and buffer-compatibility controls
secondary_readouts: Spike-in recovery percentage per fraction (qualitative assessment: recovered and membrane-protected vs not recovered)
Protein:particle ratio differences between bounded fraction and secretome control
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n 63 independent conditioned-medium lots)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: Across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots, (1) the spike-in tracer is recovered in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions and shows loss after detergent+protease (demonstrating assay function), and (2) endogenous capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity is observed reproducibly in the bounded small-EV fraction but not in the secretome-retaining concentrate processed identically. This pattern enables a pass/fail identity gate: bounded fraction = EV-enriched (pass); secretome = not EV-enriched (fail).

explicit_inferences: Inference: Spike-in recovery that is membrane-protected validates assay capture efficiency and labeling/stability, distinguishing assay failure from true absence of endogenous intact-EV signature.

Inference: Presence of an endogenous, membrane-protected, capture-positive particle peak in bounded fractions supports classifying material as EV-enriched for CMC gating; absence despite preserved spike-in recovery supports treating material as secretome.
falsification_criteria: Assay-validated outcome: preserved spike-in membrane-protected recovery in particle-peak fractions but no reproducible endogenous capture-positive co-localization and detergent/protease-sensitive signal in bounded fractions across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots (i.e., endogenous signal absent despite validated assay recovery), indicating the material is indistinguishable from secretome for identity purposes.
Assay-failure outcome: spike-in recovery is not membrane-protected or is lost inconsistently across replicates, preventing discrimination and indicating the control approach is not informative.
human_decisions_required: Approve selection and QC specifications for the exogenous intact-EV spike-in (species/tracer, concentration, QC acceptance).
Authorize use of >=3 conditioned-medium lots and associated resource allocation for orthogonal assays.
Decide whether a qualitative pass/fail identity gate is acceptable for Stage-1 advancement prior to numeric specification development.
manufacturability_assessment: Feasible at moderate complexity: spike-in addition adds procurement and QC steps but provides high-value assay control that aids comparability. Does not require numeric release limits; supports decision to adopt a bounded fraction as drug-substance if orthogonal signatures pass.
manufacturing_rationale: A non-numeric, assay-controlled identity gate based on spike-in recovery plus orthogonal co-localization reduces false negatives during scale-up and helps prioritize fractionation routes and process controls (yield, TFF envelope) without committing to numeric release limits before assay validation and pilot lots exist.
measurement_strategy: Implement paired orthogonal workflow per fraction with an exogenous intact-EV spike-in added prior to any fractionation: (1) density-gradient (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation with particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture ELISA or bead-capture + detection on intact material per fraction for canonical EV markers; (3) protease/RNase protection assays on captured material with and without detergent; (4) quantification of spike-in recovery (tracer signal) per fraction; (5) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction. Qualitative pass/fail rules: spike-in shows membrane-protected recovery in particle-peak fractions; endogenous capture-positive co-localization observed only in bounded fraction and is detergent-sensitive; secretome control fails endogenous criteria while preserving spike-in recovery.
novelty_statement: This hypothesis introduces an exogenous, characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer added prior to fractionation as an internal membrane-protection and recovery control combined with the established immuno-capture + particle-count + detergent/protease protection workflow. Prior program hypotheses proposed capture/co-localization and protection assays but did not include an internal intact-EV recovery control to rule out assay or labeling failure. The spike-in-controlled discrimination is a new, materially discriminating experiment that separates assay performance issues from true absence of endogenous intact-EV signatures and therefore provides a stronger, testable identity gate for SGL-001.
principal_risks: Spike-in EV may not mimic endogenous particle behavior, producing misleading recovery controls.
Additional assay complexity could increase sample consumption and resource needs, slowing early-stage throughput.
Even with an identity gate, cross-species delivery uncertainty (as in macaque data) may still block translational confidence.
proposed_potency_relationship: This hypothesis concerns identity only and does not assert a potency relationship. If supported, the identity gate will enable subsequent prioritized potency linkage experiments (not included here).
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt an orthogonal intact-EV identity gate operationally defined as: (A) recovery of an exogenous, characterized intact-EV spike-in that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and capture-positive fractions and (B) endogenous capture-positive signal that is detergent/protease-sensitive and co-localizes with particle peaks in the bounded fraction but not in secretome-retaining concentrates. Use the spike-in recovery readout to control for assay- and label-related loss and to enable a qualitative pass/fail identity gate (non-numeric) for defining the drug-substance as an EV-enriched small-EV fraction versus secretome.
title: Hypothesis: An orthogonal intact-EV identity gate combining spike-in protection recovery with fraction-level capture co-localization discriminates an EV-enriched drug-substance from secretome-retaining conditioned medium
